cap: A breast lump is described by breast, clock-face position and distance from the nipple, so the next examiner can find it again. The upper outer quadrant, which holds the axillary tail and the most glandular tissue, lies at 9 to 12 o'clock in the right breast and 12 to 3 o'clock in the left when the examiner faces the patient. Inspect with the arms raised and then on the hips, palpate every quadrant, then examine the axilla and the supraclavicular fossa.
teach: Both breasts are drawn as the examiner sees them, so the outer side is the left of the picture for the right breast and the right of the picture for the left breast. A clock-face position therefore names a quadrant only when the breast is stated: 2 o'clock is upper outer in the left breast, and the same quadrant is 10 o'clock in the right. Distance from the nipple in centimeters completes the address, and size, mobility and fixation describe the lump itself.
